newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russian cosmonauts begin space walk.
newsitem.headline: Two Russian cosmonauts begin space walk.

text.p: Two Russian cosmonauts from the Mir orbiting station on Monday began their second space walk in a week, a spokeswoman at the mission control centre said.
"The cosmonauts opened the station's hatch at 4.50 p.m. (0150 GMT) and began work in space," the spokeswoman said by telephone from mission control, which is just outside Moscow.
She said the cosmonauts, Valery Korzun and Alexander Koleri, planned to check and turn on a solar panel. They were expected to spend about six hours outside Mir.
The cosmonauts assembled the solar panel during another six-hour space walk on December 2.
U.S. astronaut John Blaha remained inside Mir to observe and monitor his colleagues' operations.
The spokeswoman said the U.S.-made solar panel, which was delivered to Mir by the U.S. space shuttle Atlantis last year, would provide power for Mir.
"After the cosmonauts' work, Mir will have a 100 percent power supply," the spokeswoman said.
Blaha and his two Russian colleagues have been in orbit on Mir since September 19.
